dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: *sigh* I really need this budget proposal to pass...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are...?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Ah, forgive me. I was thinking aloud. I am Euphrosiniya Ignatyevna Trubetskaya, Privy Councillor and a Veche Councillor of the Snezhnograd Veche. Please, call me Euphie.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Honestly, I would step down as councillor tomorrow if I could. After six months of watching those incompetent nobles do nothing but pass the blame around, you would understand why.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, as head of the Trubetskoy family, I cannot abandon my duties in good conscience — not while the people of Zolnyy cannot even get the ash they need to stay warm.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: If I had any real choice in the matter, I suppose I'd become a traveling merchant, or something like that... *sigh* Anything would be better than spending every day at a desk, talking myself hoarse for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are...

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Ah, forgive me. I was thinking aloud. I am Euphrosiniya Ignatyevna Trubetskaya, Privy Councillor and a Veche Councillor of the Snezhnograd Veche. Please, call me Euphie.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Honestly, I would step down as councillor tomorrow if I could. After six months of watching those incompetent nobles do nothing but pass the blame around, you would understand why.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, as head of the Trubetskoy family, I cannot abandon my duties in good conscience and stand by while people go hungry... As you know, hunger can kill. It truly can.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: If I had any real choice in the matter, I suppose I'd become a traveling merchant, or something like that... *sigh* Anything would be better than spending every day at a desk, talking myself hoarse for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I shall take my leave.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Until we meet again, outlander.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem displeased?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Indeed, I am. And if you intend to side with "The Rooster," allow me to explain. House Trubetskoy is well within its rights to say as much openly, even before Her Majesty herself.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Without question, we will forge Her Majesty's new world. But surely that does not mean the people of the old one should be left to starve and freeze in the dark.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: As a Veche Councillor, I have put forward no fewer than five proposals to improve heating in Zolnyy. But the Speaker... hah. He never fails to find some absurd excuse to dismiss them.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: If he spared even a fraction of the thought he wastes on power games for the orphans freezing in the streets, he might almost pass for human. Not that he ever was. He is a fae.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem displeased?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Indeed, I am. And if you are not familiar with how our politics work, allow me to explain. House Trubetskoy is well within its rights to say as much openly, even before Her Majesty herself.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Even now, with Project Stuzha shelved indefinitely, they still quarrel over funds that are all but meaningless to them.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: They think nothing of spending trillions of Mora on banquet halls. Yet ask them to spare a few thousand Mora per person so the poor of Zolnyy may buy food, and suddenly every coin is a matter of life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: If they refuse to pass it again, I will pay for it myself. Let them say I have some hidden agenda. Let them say I am trying to win people over. I no longer care.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About your family...

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: My house takes its name from Grand Duke Brahe Prokhorovitch Trubetskoy, Governor of Nod-Krai five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: His title came to him through his adoptive father, a fae who gave his life in glorious service to His Majesty the Belyi Tsar. Even under the laws of that time, there was nothing improper about a human inheriting a fae's title.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: When Solovei the Torchforger asked the Tsaritsa to grant the borderlands autonomy, Grand Duke Brahe also appeared before the throne. There, he willingly gave up any claim to the land and all it held.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: He then entrusted the governor's palace to the Lightkeepers, who turned it into a military fortress. And that is how the Nod-Krai we know today came to be.

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Tch... I would very much like to know which ungrateful bard in the borderlands first made up those rumors about my ancestor...

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: They claim — and please, you must not believe this — that he was made a fool of by Reed Miller's companion, and that he greedily sought some so-called "Great Treasure."

dialogues.speaker: Euphrosiniya
dialogues.text: Those lying, good-for-nothing fools are no better than the nobles on the Veche. If I ever learn who started that tale...
